name: Synthwave
description: 80s-retrofuturist arc — an arpeggiated ignition, a driving night-drive verse, a soaring gated-reverb chorus, and a guitar-like synth-lead solo.

defaults.concept: Synthwave — analog-modeled synth arpeggios, a huge gated-reverb snare, a driving sequenced bassline, and wide chorused pads under a soaring synth lead. Neon-nostalgic 80s film-score atmosphere: mechanically precise, quantized, and unswung, with wide stereo imaging.

slots.label: Arpeggio Ignition
slots.purpose: FEEL: Neon dusk, engine idling. TRICK: Let the arpeggio run alone for a few bars before the gated snare's first hit lands — that first snare crack should feel like headlights switching on.
slots.groove: Arpeggiated 16th-note synth pulse alone; gated-reverb snare hits punctuate every other bar before the full kit locks in.

slots.label: Night Drive Pocket
slots.purpose: FEEL: Driving, nocturnal, cinematic. PRODUCTION NOTE: Keep the low end mono and centered (bass plus kick) while the arpeggio and pads spread wide in stereo, for that driving-down-an-empty-highway image.
slots.groove: Driving four-on-the-floor kick (1 and 3 emphasis), gated-reverb snare cracking on 2 and 4, arpeggiated bass in steady 8ths — fully quantized, zero swing.

slots.label: The Gated Hook
slots.purpose: FEEL: Soaring, triumphant, widescreen. TRICK: Double the lead synth an octave up and drench it in the same gated-reverb chain as the snare, so the whole chorus reads as one massive hit.
slots.groove: The gated snare doubles in size (longer gate decay), a wide chorused pad blooms, and the arpeggio thickens with a second interlocking layer.

slots.label: The Synth-Lead Solo
slots.purpose: FEEL: Heroic, guitar-like defiance. PRODUCTION NOTE: Route the lead synth through light analog-style saturation and a slow pitch-bend on held notes to mimic an electric guitar solo.
slots.groove: Rhythm section holds the verse groove steady while a mono synth lead takes over with pitch-bent, guitar-like phrasing.

slots.label: Fading Signal
slots.purpose: FEEL: Fading into the neon horizon. TRICK: Automate a slow low-pass filter close over the full mix bus rather than a volume fade, so the ending feels like driving out of range of a radio signal.
slots.groove: Low-pass filter slowly closes over the arpeggio and pad until only a soft glow remains.
